# One Context Per Domain

#### Course: React Beyond Basics

## One Context Per Domain

Here's the solution to the problem we just mentioned:

ThemeContext and JournalContext are deliberately separate.

When the user toggles the theme, only components reading from ThemeContext re-render.

Components that only read JournalContext, like the entry list, are not affected at all.

![One Context Per Domain](data:application/octet-stream;base64,)

The rule is one context per domain:

- The theme state lives in ThemeContext.
- Journal data lives in JournalContext.
- If we add user authentication later, that gets its own AuthContext.

With the provider wired up and contexts properly separated, let's update the page components to consume entries from JournalContext.
